page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 959 GB SSD. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the processing and memory capabilities of this instance in the lower tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant bottleneck, with large-block read-only operations scoring in the bottom 10% at 20.18 GB/sec and write operations in the bottom 25% at 18.64 GB/sec. Data processing tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, also fall into the bottom 10% tier.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.i2ne.xlarge is its modest computational and memory throughput relative to its generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial local SSD capacity. While raw processing speeds and database operations are limited, the instance offers a high density of local storage and memory. This makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require local caching, moderate database storage, or memory-bound tasks that do not demand high CPU throughput, rather than intensive real-time web serving or heavy data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is an x86_64 server instance featuring 4 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 959 GB local SSD. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates that the instance's computational and memory performance is generally modest, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and memory bandwidth metrics consistently placing in the bottom 25% or bottom 10% tiers. Specifically, large-block memory reads and database operations show performance limitations. Consequently, this instance is best suited for workloads that prioritize local storage capacity and memory footprint over raw CPU throughput, such as localized caching, moderate database hosting, and lightweight memory-bound applications.
